title: X Feed Digest
summary: Model and research momentum: Gemini 3.1 Pro, Mercury 2 (reasoning‑diffusion LLM), and DeepMind’s AlphaEvolve highlight rapid progress in reasoning and algorithm design.
Agentic tooling is maturing across the stack, from university curricula on AI‑first development to new CLI/workflow automation for builders.
Security/data governance concerns surfaced with a DJI robot‑vacuum permissions flaw and renewed scrutiny of LLM message scraping and data releases.
Markets/news threads focused on retirement‑savings policy, enterprise software resilience to AI disruption, and the Premier League’s DTC streaming ambitions.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Gemini 3.1 Pro launch
items.body: Google announced Gemini 3.1 Pro, positioning it as a higher‑reasoning model for complex tasks beyond simple Q&A.

items.title: @StefanoErmon: Mercury 2 reasoning diffusion LLM
items.body: Mercury 2 is billed as the first reasoning‑diffusion LLM, claiming ~5× faster performance than leading speed‑optimized models.

items.title: @hasantoxr: DeepMind AlphaEvolve
items.body: Thread claims AlphaEvolve uses LLMs to mutate and evaluate algorithm code, discovering non‑intuitive improvements that beat multiple baselines on game benchmarks.

items.title: @whyyoutouzhele: DJI Romo vacuum vulnerability
items.body: Report says reverse‑engineering DJI Romo communications (via Claude Code) exposed a server‑side permissions flaw that allowed access to ~6,700 devices’ data and camera feeds; DJI says it has since patched it.

items.title: @peteromallet: Claude Code logs released
items.body: After reports that DeepSeek scraped 150k Claude messages, the author released 155k of their own Claude Code logs plus open‑source tools to export/redact data for public sharing.

items.title: @dotey: Stanford CS146S on AI‑era dev
items.body: Highlights a Stanford course on modern software development that emphasizes planning→LLM generation→editing loops, agentic tooling, code review, and automated testing with industry guest speakers.

items.title: @runes_leo: Polymarket Rust CLI for agents
items.body: Polymarket reportedly shipped an official Rust CLI aimed at AI agents; the author notes strategy and risk control are the real challenges beyond API access.

items.title: @karpathy: LLM memory+compute bottleneck
items.body: Karpathy argues token‑scale demand makes SRAM vs DRAM orchestration the key hardware constraint, with big gains possible from better training/inference pipelines.

items.title: @BillAckman: Trump Savings Plan proposal
items.body: Ackman amplifies a State‑of‑the‑Union proposal for a TSP‑style retirement plan with a federal match for workers without 401(k)s.

items.title: @BrianSozzi: Workday CEO on AI impact
items.body: Workday’s CEO says HR/ERP systems are complex systems of record and unlikely to be displaced by AI or “vibe coding” anytime soon.

items.title: @MatchDCentral: Premier League streaming plan
items.body: Report claims the Premier League is considering a direct Netflix‑style service (~£10/month, global access, and an archive of past matches).

items.title: @hxxntrr: Itemized hospital bill playbook
items.body: Advises requesting a fully itemized statement with CPT codes to surface duplicate/overpriced charges and negotiate reductions.

items.title: @geekbb: 1Password price hike
items.body: Says 1Password will raise annual pricing on Mar 27, 2026 (personal +33%, family +20%), suggesting self‑hosting Vaultwarden as an alternative.
